item.title: Kerry Hurlers In Good Health Ahead Of League Opener
item.description: Both the Kerry Senior Hurlers and Footballers get their National League campaigns underway this weekend. The hurlers are first into action on Saturday, travelling to Celtic Park to face Derry in Division 2, with throw-in at 1.30pm. Kerry manager John Griffin has been speaking to Radio Kerry commentator Andrew Morrissey ahead of the opener. Advertisement

item.title: Kerry Ladies Begin League Defense

The league champions are also away as they take on the All Ireland Champions Dublin from 2.45 at Parnell Park. item.title: Kerry taxi driver tells Oireachtas Committee that national taxi booking app is needed
item.description: The Chairman of the Tralee Taxi Association has called for the development of a national taxi booking app. Terry Boyle spoke to the Joint Committee on Transport earlier today on issues facing the taxi industry. In his opening statement he said that multinational taxi platforms, such as Uber and Bolt, have caused a decline in rural business. Advertisement He has proposed that the National Transport Authority create a taxi booking app to combat this issue: Advertisement

item.title: People in Kerry waiting for social home in own backyard told it might never happen
item.description: People in Kerry waiting for a social home in their own area are being told that it might never happen. That’s according to manager of the Killarney Municipal District, Martin O’Donoghue, who said people awaiting social housing need to be willing to move outside their own area. Figures provided at the recent Killarney MD meeting show there are 1,501 approved applicants awaiting social housing in the Killarney area. item.title: Hauliers urges local authorities to vote no confidence in RSA
item.description: The Irish Road Haulage Association is urging local authorities to submit motions of no confidence in the Road Safety Authority. Advertisement It follows Kerry County Council's decision to back such a motion. 185 people died on the roads last year, and the IRHA is calling for a re-evaluation of the RSA's role. item.title: Children's Minister Norma Foley announces multi-million Euro plan for state-led childcare centres
item.description: The new state-led childcare centres will prioritise providing places for one to three-year-olds in disadvantaged and rural areas. With a budget of 135 million euro, the government will immediately begin purchasing and renovating eight buildings into state-led early learning centres.
